items.summary: The day-3 live blog's 7:50 PM IST entry reveals the contents of the 11-petitioner writ petition filed in the SC: it seeks disclosure of internal dissents among the Election Commissioners, official minutes on voter-registration (Form 6) changes, all records related to the Special Intensive Revision (SIR), an independent audit committee, public release of deleted voters' names with reasons, an immediate stay on the ongoing SIR process, and accountability for responsible officials. First substance of the plea that the day's Chalo Dilli march was built around; contents were not public when the filing was alerted at 7:11 AM PDT.
items.title: INDIA bloc's SIR writ petition demands revealed: interim stay on SIR, public release of deleted-voter names with reasons

items.summary: The day-3 live blog's 7:43 PM IST entry reports Lok Sabha LoP Rahul Gandhi leaving the Supreme Court after filing the petition against CEC Gyanesh Kumar. Closes the day's in-court filing arc (Bhagwan Das Road stoppage -> legal team filing ~5:16 PM IST -> in-court physical filing ~7:29 PM IST). SC expected to take the plea up on Tuesday.
items.title: Rahul Gandhi leaves the Supreme Court after filing the SIR petition against CEC Gyanesh Kumar

items.source_name: thedailyjagran.com (day-3 live blog, quoting his remarks to reporters)
items.summary: Assam CM and BJP leader Himanta Biswa Sarma, speaking to reporters on the INDIA bloc's Delhi march, challenged Rahul Gandhi: ask opposition governments in Kerala, Jharkhand, Karnataka, Telangana (and the Tamil Nadu alliance government) formed during Gyanesh Kumar's tenure to resign, and announce that the opposition will not contest the upcoming Uttar Pradesh, Punjab, Goa, Manipur or Uttarakhand elections (or accept any seat) if Kumar remains CEC. Escalates his earlier X attack accusing Rahul Gandhi of selectively questioning electoral outcomes.
items.title: Himanta Biswa Sarma challenges Rahul Gandhi: resign opposition state governments, boycott elections if CEC stays
